title: Roll back Biden Interior orders and restore "Energy Dominance" agenda
proposal: The chapter says a new Administration should immediately roll back Biden's energy and climate orders at Interior, bring back the Trump-era Energy Dominance Agenda, and rescind Secretarial Order 3398.
quote: A new Administration must immediately roll back Biden’s orders, reinstate the Trump-era Energy Dominance Agenda, rescind Secretarial Order (SO) 3398

title: Reinstate a dozen Trump-era Interior secretarial orders
proposal: The chapter lists Trump-era secretarial orders to bring back right away, including ones ending the federal coal leasing moratorium, promoting offshore energy, and speeding environmental and permitting reviews.
quote: Meanwhile, the new Administration must immediately reinstate the following Trump DOI sec-retarial orders

title: Resume quarterly onshore oil and gas lease sales
proposal: The chapter says Interior should bring back quarterly onshore oil and gas lease sales in all producing states, with more public notice and comment.
quote: Reinstate quarterly onshore lease sales in all producing states according to the model of BLM’s IM 2018–034

title: Back the Lease Now and ONSHORE Acts
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should work with Congress on bills like the Lease Now Act and ONSHORE Act to give states a bigger role in energy production on federal land.
quote: ONSHORE Act,33 to increase state participation and federal accountability for energy production on the federal estate.

title: Hold as many offshore oil and gas lease sales as allowed
proposal: The chapter says Interior should hold offshore oil and gas lease sales to the maximum extent allowed under the 2023-2028 program, possibly using a previously studied alternative plan.
quote: Conduct offshore oil and natural gas lease sales to the maximum extent permitted under the 2023–2028 lease program

title: Replace five-year offshore plans with rolling lease sales
proposal: The chapter says Interior should quickly finalize a new five-year offshore plan while working with Congress to replace five-year plans with rolling or quarterly lease sales.
quote: working with Congress to reform the OCSLA by eliminating five-year plans in favor of rolling or quarterly lease sales.

title: Review recent land management plans to restore multiple use
proposal: The chapter says Interior should review land management plans finalized in the past four years and choose alternatives that restore multiple use and remove decisions advancing the "30 by 30" conservation goal.
quote: Review all resource management plans finalized in the previous four years and, when necessary, select studied alternatives to restore the multi-use concept

title: Cap federal energy lease rents, royalties and bonds
proposal: The chapter says rents, royalty rates and bonding requirements for federal leases should be set no higher than the Inflation Reduction Act requires.
quote: Set rents, royalty rates, and bonding requirements to no higher than what is required under the Inflation Reduction Act.

title: Set up oil and gas leasing in ANWR's Coastal Plain
proposal: The chapter says Interior should set up a competitive oil and gas leasing and development program in the Coastal Plain ("Section 1002 Area") of Alaska's Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.
quote: to establish a competitive leasing and development program in the Coastal Plain, an area of Alaska that was set aside by Congress specifically for future oil and gas exploration

title: Restart federal coal leasing
proposal: The chapter says Interior should finish its review of the coal leasing program and work with Wyoming and Montana leaders to restart it immediately.
quote: Conclude the programmatic review of the coal leasing program, and work with the congressional delegations and governors of Wyoming and Montana to restart the program immediately.

title: Drop leasing bans at Thompson Divide, Chaco and Boundary Waters
proposal: The chapter says Interior should abandon plans to close lands to leasing in Colorado's Thompson Divide, a 10-mile buffer around Chaco in New Mexico, and the Boundary Waters in Minnesota, if not yet completed.
quote: Abandon withdrawals of lands from leasing in the Thompson Divide of the White River National Forest, Colorado; the 10-mile buffer around Chaco

title: Speed federal drilling and right-of-way permits
proposal: The chapter says Interior's regional offices should finish right-of-way and drilling permits as fast as states in the region typically do.
quote: Require regional offices to complete right-of-way and drilling permits within the average time it takes states in the region to complete them.

title: Restore Trump rules on methane waste, critical habitat, birds and NEPA
proposal: The chapter says Interior should rescind Biden rules and reinstate Trump rules on BLM waste prevention, Endangered Species Act critical habitat, the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, and CEQ's NEPA reforms.
quote: Rescind the Biden rules and reinstate the Trump rules regarding: 1. BLM waste prevention; 2. The Endangered Species Act rules defining Critical Habitat

title: Open most of Alaska's National Petroleum Reserve to drilling
proposal: The chapter says Interior should reinstate the Trump plan (the 2020 Integrated Activity Plan) opening most of the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska to leasing and development.
quote: Reinstate President Trump’s plan for opening most of the National Petroleum Reserve of Alaska to leasing and development.

title: Bring back Schedule F for Interior employees
proposal: The chapter says President Trump's Schedule F proposal, which makes it easier to fire some federal employees, must be reinstated, including at the Office of Surface Mining.
quote: President Trump’s Schedule F proposal44 regarding accountability in hiring must be reinstituted to bring success to these reforms.

title: Expand state and tribal land management agreements
proposal: The chapter says Interior should look for chances to expand cooperative agreements with states and tribes.
quote: DOI should also look for opportunities to broaden state–federal and tribal–federal cooperative agreements.

title: Move BLM headquarters back to the West
proposal: The chapter says the Bureau of Land Management's headquarters belongs in the West and criticizes the move of its leaders back to Washington, D.C.
quote: BLM headquarters belongs in the American West. After all, the overwhelming majority of the 245 million surface acres

title: Put BLM law officers under a law enforcement chain of command
proposal: The chapter says BLM law enforcement rangers and agents should report only to law enforcement supervisors, as the Inspector General recommended, rather than to land managers.
quote: They should report to a professional, expert, and knowledgeable chain of command.

title: Let BLM humanely put down excess wild horses and burros
proposal: The chapter says Congress must pass laws allowing the BLM to dispose of excess wild horses and burros humanely.
quote: Congress must enact laws permitting the BLM to dispose humanely of these animals.

title: Revoke old federal land orders blocking Alaska land transfers
proposal: The chapter says BLM land orders blocking Alaska and Alaska Natives from selecting land owed to them should be lifted, starting with PLO 5150, and all other old orders revoked immediately.
quote: All other remaining BLM PLOs—all of which are more than 50 years old—should be revoked immediately.

title: Reinstate 2020 ANWR study and lift lease suspensions
proposal: The chapter says Interior should reinstate the 2020 Arctic National Wildlife Refuge environmental impact statement by secretarial order and lift the suspension of leases there.
quote: Reinstate the 2020 Arctic National Wildlife Refuge Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) by secretarial order and lift the suspension of the leases.

title: Approve Willow oil project with five drilling pads
proposal: The chapter says Interior should approve the 2020 Willow project plan in Alaska's petroleum reserve and expand it from three to five drilling pads.
quote: Approve the 2020 Willow EIS, the largest pending oil and gas projection in the United States in the National Petroleum Reserve-Alaska, and expand approval from three to five drilling pads.

title: Approve the Ambler Road mining project in Alaska
proposal: The chapter says Interior should immediately approve the 211-mile Ambler Road across BLM land to open an area of Alaska to mining.
quote: the new Administration must immedi-ately approve the Ambler Road Project 60 across BLM-managed lands

title: Revoke federal predator control and bear baiting rules in Alaska
proposal: The chapter says National Park Service and Fish and Wildlife Service rules on predator control and bear baiting in Alaska should be revoked, leaving these matters to the state.
quote: Revoke National Park Service and U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service rules regarding predator control and bear baiting, which are matters for state regulation.

title: Let Alaska manage fish and game on federal lands
proposal: The chapter says Interior should recognize Alaska's authority to manage fish and game on all federal lands in the state.
quote: Recognize Alaska’s authority to manage fish and game on all federal lands in accordance with ANILCA as during the Reagan Administration

title: Declare Alaska owns lands under its navigable waters
proposal: The chapter says Interior should issue an order declaring navigable waters in Alaska to be state-owned, putting the burden on BLM to prove a waterway is not navigable.
quote: Issue a secretarial order declaring navigable waters in Alaska to be owned by the state so that the lands beneath these waters belong to Alaska.

title: Reinstate the 2020 Alaska Roadless Rule for the Tongass
proposal: The chapter says the Trump 2020 Alaska Roadless Rule for the Tongass National Forest should be reinstated, replacing the current rule that limits roads and logging.
quote: Reinstate President Trump’s 2020 Alaska Roadless Rule64 for the Tongass National Forest in Alaska

title: Cancel the "30 by 30" conservation order
proposal: The chapter says the President should vacate Executive Order 14008's "30 by 30" plan to conserve 30 percent of U.S. lands and waters by 2030, and Interior should act against it immediately.
quote: Although the new President should vacate that order, DOI under a conservative President must take immediate action on the 30 by 30 plan

title: Require state and local approval for federal land purchases
proposal: The chapter says Interior should vacate a Biden order that removed the requirement for state and local approval before the federal government buys private land with Land and Water Conservation Fund money.
quote: vacating a secre-tarial order issued by the Biden DOI69 that eliminated the Trump Administration’s requirement for the approval of state and local governments

title: Review and shrink national monuments
proposal: The chapter says the new Administration should review past and Biden national monument designations, reduce some (such as in Maine and Oregon), and defend those reductions up to the Supreme Court.
quote: the new Administration must vigorously defend the downward adjustments it makes to permit a ruling on a President’s authority to reduce the size of national monuments

title: Repeal the Antiquities Act
proposal: The chapter says the new Administration should ask Congress to repeal the Antiquities Act of 1906, which lets presidents create national monuments.
quote: Finally, the new Administration must seek repeal of the Antiquities Act of 1906

title: Manage Oregon O&C lands for timber harvest
proposal: The chapter says Interior must manage Oregon's O&C federal lands for permanent timber production so the timber is sold and cut, as the 1937 law directs.
quote: fulfill its responsibilities and manage the O&C lands for “permanent forest production” to ensure that the timber is “sold, cut, and removed.

title: Restore Interior limits on length and time of NEPA reviews
proposal: The chapter says Interior should reinstate Trump-era orders putting time and page limits on environmental review documents and listing each document's cost on page one.
quote: DOI should reinstate the secretarial orders adopted by the Trump Administration, such as placing time and page limits on

title: Ask Congress to reform NEPA and limit court review
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should ask Congress to reform the National Environmental Policy Act, including considering ending court review of NEPA documents and decisions.
quote: Consideration should be given, for example, to eliminat-ing judicial review of the adequacy of NEPA documents or the rectitude of NEPA decisions.

title: Publish Interior legal settlements and attorney fees
proposal: The chapter says Interior should bring back a policy of publicly posting all litigation settlements and attorney fees paid.
quote: would cause controversy, ended this policy.81 A new Administration should reinstate it.

title: Ask Congress to reform the Endangered Species Act
proposal: The chapter says Congress should reform the Endangered Species Act to stop it from being used to take private property, block economic development or override states' wildlife authority.
quote: Meaningful reform of the Endangered Species Act requires that Congress take action to restore its original purpose

title: Remove grizzly bears from the endangered list
proposal: The chapter says grizzly bears in the Greater Yellowstone and Northern Continental Divide areas should be removed from Endangered Species Act protection, and the decision defended up to the Supreme Court.
quote: Delist the grizzly bear in the Greater Yellowstone and Northern Continental Divide Ecosystems

title: Remove gray wolves from the endangered list
proposal: The chapter says the gray wolf in the lower 48 states should be removed from Endangered Species Act protection.
quote: Delist the gray wolf in the lower 48 states in light of its full recovery under the ESA.

title: Hand sage-grouse management to western states
proposal: The chapter says Interior should give western states authority over the greater sage-grouse.
quote: Cede to western states jurisdiction over the greater sage-grouse, recognizing the on-the-ground expertise of states

title: Limit "experimental" species reintroductions
proposal: The chapter says the Fish and Wildlife Service should stop reintroducing "experimental" species populations into areas outside their historic range or no longer suitable habitat.
quote: Direct the Fish and Wildlife Service to end its abuse of Section 10( j) of the ESA

title: Create a conservation "triage" program
proposal: The chapter says the Fish and Wildlife Service should prioritize limited conservation money where it achieves the most results.
quote: Direct the Fish and Wildlife Service to design and implement an impartial conservation triage program

title: Make all endangered species decision data public
proposal: The chapter says the Fish and Wildlife Service should publish all data used in Endangered Species Act decisions, with few or no exceptions.
quote: Direct the Fish and Wildlife Service to make all data used in ESA decisions available to the public

title: Abolish USGS Biological Resources Division
proposal: The chapter says the U.S. Geological Survey's Biological Resources Division should be abolished and species research obtained from universities through competitive bids.
quote: Abolish the Biological Resources Division of the U.S. Geological Survey and obtain necessary scientific research about species of concern from universities

title: End reliance on "species specialists" in ESA decisions
proposal: The chapter says the Fish and Wildlife Service should stop relying on species specialists it views as biased and follow the Information Quality Act.
quote: ensures independent decision-making by ending reliance on so-called species specialists

title: Move surface mining office headquarters to Pittsburgh
proposal: The chapter says the Office of Surface Mining's headquarters should move to Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, to be in coal country.
quote: Relocate the OSM Reclamation and Enforcement headquarters to Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania

title: Cut the number of coal mine inspectors
proposal: The chapter says the number of field coal-reclamation inspectors should be reduced because the coal industry is smaller.
quote: Reduce the number of field coal-reclamation inspectors to recognize the industry is smaller.

title: Open surface mining training to coal company workers
proposal: The chapter says coal company employees should be allowed to use the OSM Training Program, now limited to state and federal workers.
quote: Permit coal company employees to benefit from the OSM Training Program, which is currently restricted to state and federal employees.

title: Let mining regulators weigh extenuating circumstances
proposal: The chapter says the Applicant Violator System database should be revised so regulators can consider extenuating circumstances.
quote: Revise the Applicant Violator System, the nationwide database for the federal and state programs, to permit federal and state regulators to consider extenuating circumstances.

title: Add western water storage capacity
proposal: The chapter says the Bureau of Reclamation should develop more water storage in the arid West, including by updating dam manuals and monitoring operations in real time.
quote: Develop additional storage capacity across the arid west, including by: 1. Updating dam water control manuals for existing facilities

title: Consolidate federal water working groups
proposal: The chapter says the Bureau of Reclamation should combine federal water working groups to reduce inefficiency.
quote: Reduce bureaucratic inefficiencies by consolidating federal water working groups.

title: Improve water supply forecasting
proposal: The chapter says the Bureau of Reclamation should carry out the Federal Action Plan for Improving Forecasts of Water Availability, including forecast-informed reservoir operations and aerial snow observation.
quote: Implement actions identified in the Federal Action Plan for Improving Fore-casts of Water Availability

title: Clarify the water infrastructure loan program
proposal: The chapter says the Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act should be clarified to match other federal infrastructure loan programs and encourage local investment.
quote: Clarify the Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act94 to ensure consistent application with other federal infrastructure loan programs

title: Reinstate Trump memo on western water supply
proposal: The chapter says the Presidential Memorandum on Promoting the Reliable Supply and Delivery of Water in the West should be reinstated.
quote: Reinstate Presidential Memorandum on Promoting the Reliable Supply and Delivery of Water in the West.

title: Support energy and mineral development on tribal lands
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should help develop fossil fuels and minerals on lands owned by American Indians and tribes.
quote: End the war on fossil fuels and domestically available minerals and facilitate their development on lands owned by Indians and Indian nations.

title: End federal electric vehicle mandates and subsidies
proposal: The chapter says federal mandates and subsidies for electric vehicles should end.
quote: End federal mandates and subsidies of electric vehicles.

title: Restore tribal authority over environmental rules on tribal land
proposal: The chapter says tribal governments' right to enforce environmental regulations on their own lands should be restored.
quote: Restore the right of tribal governments to enforce environmental regulation on their lands.

title: Overhaul Bureau of Indian Education schools
proposal: The chapter says Bureau of Indian Education schools should be overhauled to put parents and children first; it also faults the bureau for not reporting student test data.
quote: Overhaul BIE schools to put parents and their children first.

title: Reauthorize the tribal Land Buy-Back Program
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should ask Congress to reauthorize the Land Buy-Back Program for Tribal Nations, paid for with Great American Outdoors Act money.
quote: the new Administration should seek congressional reauthorization of the Land Buy-Back Program for Tribal Nations
